question: What is the calculated molecular mass of oxygen?
solution:
The correct answer is __**32**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The molecular mass of oxygen (O₂) is calculated by adding the atomic masses of two oxygen atoms.
 
• The atomic mass of one oxygen atom is approximately 16 atomic mass units (amu).
 
• Therefore, the molecular mass of O₂ is 16 amu + 16 amu = 32 amu.
 
• This value is based on the atomic mass unit scale, where 1 amu is defined as one-twelfth the mass of a carbon-12 atom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Molecular Mass**

 
 
• Molecular mass is the sum of the masses of all the atoms in a molecule.
 
• It is commonly measured in atomic mass units (amu) or Daltons (Da).
 
 
 
• **Oxygen Gas (O₂)**
 
 
• Oxygen is a diatomic molecule, meaning it consists of two oxygen atoms bonded together.
 
• It is essential for respiration in most living organisms and is used in various industrial processes.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Mass Unit (amu)**
 
 
• 1 atomic mass unit is defined as one-twelfth the mass of a carbon-12 atom, approximately 1.66053906660 × 10⁻²⁷ kg.
 
• This unit is used to express the mass of atoms and molecules.
 
 
 
• **Avogadro's Number**
 
 
• Avogadro's number (6.02214076 × 10²³) is the number of atoms, ions, or molecules in one mole of a substance.
 
• It is used to convert between atomic mass units and grams.
